The WEB quotation opens at web:Ps.132.3 (“Surely I will not come into the structure of my house”) and closes at the end of web:Ps.132.5 (“...a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”), confirmed by direct reading of verse_map_web.json; unquoted material resumes at web:Ps.132.6, which the row correctly treats as its far seam and lists in boundary_evidence_refs along with web:Ps.132.7. All four Hebrew quotes cited in this row's rationale and observed_substrate_signals collate at byte tier against verse_map_oshb.json (verified via collate.py --json). Ps 132 is an identity psalm in web_mt_offset_map.json (rule=identity), so web:Ps.132.0 = oshb:Ps.132.1 is the correct dual-cite form for the title. pmarks_Ps.json carries zero Ps.132 selah entries, so the span-scoped absence claim is valid. rejected_alternative is a single sentence grounded in the actual clause continuation from 132:1 into 132:2 (no fresh vocative or quotation boundary), confirmed by direct reading -- 132:2 continues 'how he swore to Yahweh, and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:' without a new address. unit_type=strophe and confidence=high are calibrated to the strength of the quotation-boundary evidence. citation_sweep.py, check_refs_mirror.py, check_web_quotes.py, check_marks.py and check_tiling.py all return GREEN for this row within the cluster batch.

Re-derived the addressee structure of web:Ps.132.6-Ps.132.10 directly from verse_map_web.json and verse_map_oshb.json rather than trusting the row's characterization. The row's rationale calls the span 'one liturgical movement addressed to Yahweh', and its rejected_alternative rejects splitting the vow (132:6-7) from the petition (132:8-10) because 'both remain addressed to the same second-person Yahweh'. That claim is not accurate for 132:6-7: oshb:Ps.132.7's two verbs govern third-person masculine singular suffixes (matching WEB's own 'his dwelling place... his footstool', web:Ps.132.7) -- there is no second-person address to Yahweh anywhere in 132:6-7. Direct second-person vocative address to Yahweh first appears at oshb:Ps.132.8's opening imperative-plus-vocative, continuing with two second-person masculine singular possessive suffixes, matching web:Ps.132.8's 'Arise, Yahweh, into your resting place, you, and the ark of your strength.' Both half-verses collate at byte tier (collate.py --json, verse_map_oshb.json). This is a real, Hebrew-confirmed addressee shift (third-person reference to Yahweh in 132:6-7 versus direct second-person vocative address beginning at 132:8) coinciding with a WEB quotation close at the end of 132:7 -- exactly the kind of tier-1 signal (addressee shift plus quotation boundary) this cluster's sibling rows (437, 439, 440) treat as decisive when it occurs at their own seams (132:2/3, 132:5/6, 132:10/11, 132:13/14). The row does not have to adopt the rival split -- there is a legitimate case that 132:6-10 forms one unbroken liturgical movement (search, vow, invocation, petition) with no intervening REPORT clause comparable to 132:6's own opening, which is the row's other, textually sound argument -- but the specific warrant given ('both remain addressed to the same second-person Yahweh') misstates the grammar of the very verses it is citing, and the row's own rationale repeats the same overstatement. citation_sweep.py, check_refs_mirror.py, check_web_quotes.py and check_tiling.py return GREEN for the row's mechanical layer (refs, quotes, tiling); this challenge is a content/warrant defect, not a mechanical one.

challenges.claim: The row's warrant for keeping web:Ps.132.6-Ps.132.10 as one strophe -- that 132:6-7 and 132:8-10 are 'addressed to the same second-person Yahweh' -- misstates the addressee grammar: 132:6-7 refer to Yahweh only in the third person, and second-person vocative address begins only at 132:8, which is itself a tier-1 addressee-shift signal the row's own methodology treats as decisive elsewhere in this psalm.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.132.7 (byte-collated): “נָב֥וֹאָה לְמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֑יו נִ֝שְׁתַּחֲוֶ֗ה לַהֲדֹ֥ם רַגְלָֽיו” -- both verbs carry the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix meaning 'his': the first on 'dwelling place(s)', the second on 'feet' inside the phrase rendered 'his footstool' -- matching WEB “We will go into his dwelling place. We will worship at his footstool.” (web:Ps.132.7) -- no second-person form and no vocative anywhere in the verse. oshb:Ps.132.8 (byte-collated): “קוּמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לִמְנוּחָתֶ֑ךָ אַ֝תָּ֗ה וַאֲר֥וֹן עֻזֶּֽךָ” -- opens with the vocative divine name immediately after the imperative 'arise', then carries two second-person masculine singular possessive suffixes meaning 'your': on 'resting place' and on 'strength' -- matching WEB “Arise, Yahweh, into your resting place, you, and the ark of your strength.” (web:Ps.132.8). Both verses collate at byte tier (collate.py --json against verse_map_oshb.json, 2 of 2 GREEN). The two verses' finite-verb-plus-suffix constructions are opposite in grammatical person (third in 132:7 vs second in 132:8), so the row's 'both...second-person Yahweh' claim covering 132:6-7 is not supported by either witness.

reviews.reasoning: Independently re-derived rather than trusting the row. The claimed verb-form echo between oshb:Ps.132.2 and oshb:Ps.132.11 was checked byte-for-byte: 132:2's second word and 132:11's first word are both the Niphal perfect 3ms of the root meaning 'to swear' ('he has sworn'); accent-stripped comparison shows a meteg-only difference (132:11's form carries a meteg the 132:2 form lacks), while the consonantal skeleton is identical. The row's own qualifier ('same inflected form, not claimed to govern the whole row') is accurate and properly hedged -- it does not overclaim byte-identity. The person-shift claim at the 132:13|14 seam was independently checked at the Hebrew level: 132:13's two verbs ('he chose', 'he desired') are third-person masculine singular, while 132:14's verbs ('I will sit/dwell', 'I have desired it') are first-person common singular, confirming the claimed report/oracle person shift exactly where the WEB quotation mark opens (end of 132:13, unquoted; start of 132:14, quoted through the psalm's close). Both cited Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier. pmarks_Ps.json carries zero Ps.132 selah entries, so the absence claim is valid. The rejected_alternative is a single sentence that discloses the genuine rival (attaching 132:13 to the following oracle) and gives a textually grounded reason for preferring the quotation-marked seam at 132:13|14 over 132:12|13; confidence=medium is well-calibrated to how close this call actually is. citation_sweep.py, check_refs_mirror.py, check_web_quotes.py and check_tiling.py all return GREEN.

The Hebrew title-line quote for 132:14 collates at byte tier. The person-shift argument distinguishing this row's first-person oracle from 132:13's third-person report was independently re-derived at the Hebrew level under M8-Ps-439's review (132:13 verbs = 3ms; 132:14 verbs = 1cs) and confirms this row's seam is correctly placed. pmarks_Ps.json carries zero Ps.132 selah entries, validating the span-scoped absence claim. rejected_alternative is a single sentence, correctly grounded in the same person/quotation-mark distinction. citation_sweep.py, check_refs_mirror.py, check_web_quotes.py and check_tiling.py all return GREEN.
